review: Recovery53 reuse of a completed strict whole-profile validation pass
changeAssessment: Only private whole-profile column and string-table iterators enable validated decoding. The initial complete document cursor and JSONL decoding retain strict duplicate-key, nonfinite-number, UTF8, grammar and bound validation.

The whole document is validated through its trailing EOF before metadata/schema and any array iteration. The indexed spans and counts remain tied to the same already-open descriptor; no independent pathname open is added.

The validated pass uses the ordinary bounded decoder and avoids repeating container-bound walks and number/key hooks on data already validated. This includes bounded scalar fallback values as well as the 64 KiB fast chunks; individual raw values remain limited to 1 MiB.

Marker schema, finite times, integer indices, phase/end relationships, column cardinality, aggregate bounds and fixed public target names remain independently enforced. The unchanged final FD/path/directory and ctime/mtime/size identities must match before any aggregate result is published.

A file change between validation and aggregation yields unconfirmed coverage and null counts. This preserves the declared trusted single-purpose-runner contract; it does not introduce a claim of an atomic snapshot or protection against arbitrary hostile same-UID rewriting.

The same 195000385-byte input and SHA256, one million resource rows, 30-second cooperative budget, assertion frame 450, caps, clocks, resource limits and diagnostic continuation/final-failure semantics remain unchanged.

candidateRoute.existingNegativeAndFlowControls: Recovery52 controls may be inherited through the exact unchanged gate bodies; they were not redundantly rerun for this label-only candidate.

precisionAndRemainingGate: Linux phase observations and the faster Linux collector result support testing reduced repeat work; they do not establish which pass exhausted the budget on either actual Mac run.
Recovery52 reached the same processing guard after the primitive-prefix optimization. A budget-censored result cannot quantify improvement or prove the optimization had no effect.

Actual Intel Mac dense-input qualification remains unproven for this candidate. One short diagnostic requires immutable source/caller readback, no owned-job overlap, an unused branch and the unchanged strict gates.

An isolated density failure may continue to independent recording and serializer observations only under the inherited exact safety predicate; it must retain the original first failure and final failed job.

No new long build or product/Mozilla/native qualification follows from this source review. Recovery48 stopped at its known shared345 full-build deadline; unfinished compiler subphase and remaining work are unknown, and the original native exit cause remains unknown.
